articles.title_original: In Amish country, nurses go door to door to stop deadly spread of measles
articles.title_zh: In Amish country, nurses go door to door to stop deadly spread of measles
facts_zh:
In Amish country, nurses go door to door to stop deadly spread of measles
- Published
For the past few months, nurse Dale Weiser has been making unexpected home visits.

As the state battles the deadliest measles outbreak in recent history, the clinical supervisor drives 30 miles (48.3km), sometimes daily, to a rural corner of Pennsylvania where many Amish people live.
Walking into strangers' homes, Weiser says she tries her best to be respectful and non-intrusive as she vaccinates dozens of family members against the measles, sometimes around the kitchen table.

all_titles.en: In Amish country, nurses go door to door to stop deadly spread of measles

articles.title_zh: AI superpower ambitions take centre stage as Trump and Xi meet
facts_zh:
AI superpower ambitions take centre stage as Trump and Xi meet
- Published
"Whoever wins AI, WINS!"
US President Donald Trump has been blunt about his AI ambitions, as well as about who he considers the US's main rival to be: China.
His Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, has not said anything so forthright - but it seems he holds a similar view.

"China very much sees it as a race, they very much think China should be the leading force in AI - they see AI as a power maximiser," says Rebecca Arcesati, from the Mercator Institute for China Studies.

all_titles.en: AI superpower ambitions take centre stage as Trump and Xi meet

articles.title_zh: Trump's Board of Peace unveils $2.45bn plan to begin Gaza's reconstruction
facts_zh:
Trump's Board of Peace unveils $2.45bn plan to begin Gaza's reconstruction
- Published
US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace has announced a Gaza recovery plan worth $2.45bn (£1.85bn) during a meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
The funding will be spread across 66 programmes over six months, and directed at housing, diesel generation and waste removal, among other needs.
But the board admitted substantial donations were still needed, with $18bn pledged but only $280m handed over so far.

all_titles.en: Trump's Board of Peace unveils $2.45bn plan to begin Gaza's reconstruction

articles.title_original: UK survivor of Canadian poison seller says he exploited her despair
articles.title_zh: UK survivor of Canadian poison seller says he exploited her despair
facts_zh:
UK survivor of Canadian poison seller says he exploited her despair
- Published
A British woman, one of the survivors of Canadian poison seller Kenneth Law, faced him in court on Wednesday to describe how he had exploited her vulnerability.
Elisabeth Belien told the four-day sentencing hearing of Law in Ontario, Canada she had been at her lowest ebb when he sold her toxic chemicals when she was just 23.
Belien, who until Wednesday had not been known as one of his customers, said she had physically recovered after being successfully given an antidote by medics.

all_titles.en: UK survivor of Canadian poison seller says he exploited her despair

articles.title_original: Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war
articles.title_zh: Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war
facts_zh:
Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war
- Published
Ethiopia's government and the party in control of the northern region of Tigray have accused each other of launching offensives, escalating fears of a return to full-scale conflict.

Getachew Reda, a cabinet minister and adviser to Ethiopia's prime minister, said Tigrayan fighters had taken control of federally administered airports in Tigray and launched offensives in neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions.
Earlier, the Tigrayan authorities said their forces had been forced to enter a "defensive war".

all_titles.en: Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war

articles.title_original: Eleven killed in mass shooting at house in South Africa
articles.title_zh: Eleven killed in mass shooting at house in South Africa
facts_zh:
Eleven killed in mass shooting at house in South Africa
- Published
At least 11 people have been killed in a mass shooting in a residential building near the South African city of Durban.
Gunmen stormed a house in the KwaMakhutha township late on Tuesday and opened fire on 14 people.
Ten were killed at the scene and four were taken to hospital, where one later died from their injuries, police said.

all_titles.en: Eleven killed in mass shooting at house in South Africa
